sources.entry: langgraph - Low-level orchestration framework for building stateful, long-running LLM agents.
LangGraph — Graph-based stateful agent orchestration from the LangChain team. Suited for complex, cyclic agent workflows. MIT.

summary.one_liner: LangGraph is a low-level Python orchestration framework from LangChain Inc for building stateful, long-running LLM agents and workflows.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LangGraph as infrastructure for building, managing, and deploying long-running, stateful agents and workflows. It highlights durable execution, where agents persist through failures and resume where they left off. It supports human-in-the-loop oversight by letting users inspect and modify agent state during execution. It offers short-term working memory and long-term persistent memory across sessions. It works standalone and also integrates with LangChain, LangSmith for tracing and evals, and LangSmith Deployment. The README also points to a JS/TS counterpart, LangGraph.js, and to Deep Agents, a higher-level package built on LangGraph.
use_cases: add human-in-the-loop review to agent workflows
resume agents after failures or crashes
give agents short-term and long-term memory
debug and trace agent execution paths
notable: Durable execution that resumes agents from where they left off after failures
Human-in-the-loop by inspecting and modifying agent state mid-run
Inspired by Pregel and Apache Beam, with a public interface drawing on NetworkX
caveats: Low-level framework: building agents may require more code than higher-level packages such as Deep Agents, which the README points to
Some deployment and debugging features are tied to LangSmith products, which the README presents as separate offerings
